questions.title: Who will win the women's singles title at the 2026 Canadian Open?
questions.background: The Canadian Open is a major hard-court tennis tournament held during the build-up to the US Open.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The official WTA results for the 2026 Canadian Open will determine the women's singles champion. Resolution Timing : The question resolves when the tournament's women's singles final is completed and its result is officially recorded. Accepted Answer Format : Provide the winning player's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Official July 31 Toronto National Bank Open draw (wtatennis.com, nationalbankopen.com) eliminates pre-US Open skip risk for World No. 1 Aryna Sabalenka and World No. 2 Elena Rybakina, with all top-10 healthy stars entered (confirmed withdrawals: Victoria Mboko, Karolina Muchova, Jasmine Paolini, Emma Raducanu). Sabalenka rises 0.17 -> 0.21 as confirmed #1 seed in a clean Q1 (Ostapenko R3, Alexandrova/Chwalinska R4, Anisimova/Svitolina QF; 6-1 H2H vs Svitolina) with zero skip discount. Rybakina ticks up 0.13 -> 0.14 as #2 seed in the bottom half (avoiding Sabalenka/Swiatek/Pegula until final; opens vs Kasatkina/Wang -> Ann Li -> Cirstea/Krejcikova). Coco Gauff holds 0.09 and climbs to #3 in a favorable Q3 where Wimbledon champ Linda Noskova (#6) and red-hot Alexandra Eala (#25) collide in R3. Jessica Pegula drops 0.10 -> 0.08 after reaching the Aug 2 Washington Open final vs Eala (tight turnaround/fatigue and modest withdrawal risk) and landing in a brutal Q2 alongside Iga Swiatek (#7, already on site), Marta Kostyuk (#10, 2-0 vs Pegula in 2026), and Diana Shnaider (#15), with Sabalenka looming in the SF. Mirra Andreeva trims 0.08 -> 0.07 facing a difficult Q4 path (Fernandez -> 2025 finalist Osaka -> Rybakina). Top-5 sum = 0.59, preserving 0.41 outside for Swiatek (~0.07), Noskova (~0.05), Kostyuk (~0.035), Osaka (~0.035), Anisimova (~0.03), and wide WTA 1000 variance.

local_articles.title: Aryna Sabalenka aims to bounce back in Toronto after Wimbledon disappointment
local_articles.snippet: TORONTO – Aryna Sabalenka’s world No. 1 ranking will be on the line at the WTA 1000 tournament in Toronto, where the Belarusian star aims to extend her hard court dominance in the build-up to her US Open title defence. Sabalenka has won 23 of her 24 hard court matches in 2026, the lone defeat her loss to Elena Rybakina in the Australian Open final. But she was turfed out in the quarter-finals on the clay of Roland Garros and fell to Naomi Osaka in the round of 16 on the grass courts of Wimbledon. The breakthrough title will propel Eala to a career-high world number 20 when the new WTA rankings are released. REUTERS

local_articles.title: Rain forces Washington Open final to be rescheduled, Canadian Open play also pushed back
local_articles.snippet: The Washington Open women's final between Jessica Pegula and Alexandra Eala was suspended in the second set and pushed back to Monday due to rain, while matches at the Canadian Open in Toronto and Montreal were also rescheduled due to the weather. The Washington final was delayed by three hours before play got under way on Sunday, with American Pegula taking the opening set 6-4 and the Philippines' Eala leading 2-1 in the second when the match was halted due to rain. The men's final between American Taylor Fritz and Spain's Rafael Jodar was also moved to Monday. "Matches have been cancelled for tonight. The women’s singles final will now take place at 12:00 p.m. tomorrow. The men’s singles final will take place not before 1:00 p.m. tomorrow," tournament organisers said on social media. questions.title: Which two countries will reach the final of the 2026 Women's Africa Cup of Nations?
questions.background: The Women's Africa Cup of Nations is Africa's continental championship for women's national football teams. The winners of its two semifinals advance to the final.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : CAF's official tournament results, supported where necessary by contemporaneous match reporting. Resolution : Resolve once both semifinals of the 2026 Women's Africa Cup of Nations have concluded and the two finalists have been determined. The result of the final itself is not relevant. Accepted Answer Format : The two finalist country names in alphabetical order, separated by a comma.
questions.current_reasoning: Massive WAFCON 2026 bracket realignment after Aug 1-2 MD2 results (CAFonline, beIN SPORTS, Sportblot, BSS/AFP): (1) Half 1 (A1/B2/D1/C2) has become a loaded gauntlet housing Morocco (6 pts, beat Algeria 1-0 to clinch QF and ~93% A1), Cameroon (6 pts, beat Ghana 1-0 on Sunday Aug 2 to lock ~99% QF / ~97% D1), AND Nigeria (beat Zambia 1-0 with 10 women on Saturday Aug 1; now ~95% to advance by beating winless Egypt on MD3, and nearly mathematically locked into C2 under CAF H2H tiebreakers since Malawi already has 6 pts and beat Nigeria 3-2, while a 2+ goal Zambia win over Malawi would put Zambia C1 and Nigeria C2). Consequently, previous top-5 finals Morocco-Nigeria (0.07) and Cameroon-Morocco (0.06) collapse to <1% since all three share Half 1, while Morocco-Zambia (0.09) collapses to ~2.5% because Zambia now faces ~75% group-stage elimination (even a 1-0/2-1/3-2 win over Malawi eliminates Zambia on the 3-way H2H mini-table if Nigeria beats Egypt!). (2) Half 2 (B1/A2/C1/D2) is now dominated by Malawi (~80% C1 on 6 pts after beating Egypt 3-1), Ghana (~73% D2 after losing 0-1 to Cameroon, needing a result vs Mali Aug 6), Ivory Coast (~72% B1 on 4 pts, +3 GD), and Algeria (~91% A2). A 4-model ensemble Monte Carlo (160,000 sims with exact CAF H2H tiebreakers) elevates Malawi, Morocco (0.09), Ghana, Morocco (0.09), Malawi, Nigeria (0.08 — Group C rematch across opposite halves!), Ghana, Nigeria (0.08), and Ivory Coast, Morocco (0.07) into the top 5 (sum 0.41, leaving 59% across Algeria-Morocco ~0.07, Ivory Coast-Nigeria ~0.055, Algeria-Nigeria ~0.05, Cameroon finals, etc.).

questions.title: Which European country will announce a complete drought-related shutdown of its nuclear power generation between August 1 and August 13, 2026?
questions.background: Nuclear reactors require reliable cooling-water supplies. Low river levels can force reactors to shut down, potentially disrupting national electricity supplies.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official announcements by national nuclear operators or governments, corroborated by reliable news reporting. Resolution Conditions : Identify the European country that announces, between August 1 and August 13, 2026, a shutdown covering its entire operating nuclear fleet because drought has left insufficient river water for cooling. An announcement initiating the shutdown of the last operating reactor qualifies; a partial shutdown alone does not. Accepted Answer Format : The country's common English name.
questions.current_reasoning: Major Aug 1-2 breaking news across Reuters, Bloomberg, Al Jazeera, CE Energy News, and IBNA: (1) Hungary surges 0.34 -> 0.68: PM Peter Magyar announced on Saturday Aug 1 and Sunday Aug 2 that Hungary is completely shutting down its sole nuclear plant (Paks) for the first time in 44 years due to record-low Danube levels; the second-to-last unit shut at 1:30 a.m. Aug 2, leaving the final unit at ~240 MW (>10% capacity) as of 18:37 GMT Sunday Aug 2 with Magyar stating Paks will not generate tomorrow (Aug 3) and plant management will initiate final shutdown under security protocol — matching the Aug 1-13 window and 'initiating the shutdown of the last operating reactor' clause directly. Capped at 0.68 (not >0.85) because Hungary's earlier July 30-31 announcements already resolved sister QID 683823, leaving genuine criteria/overlap risk if Romania also shuts down its last unit. (2) Romania trims 0.34 -> 0.25 but remains a live #2: Cernavoda Unit 1 is offline while Unit 2 still operates under a July 31 state of alert, but CE Energy News (Aug 2) reports Sunday's military rock-blasting at Parjoaia to divert Danube flow failed (another attempt planned Monday Aug 3) and Nuclearelectrica warned partners of potential force majeure. (3) Bulgaria slashes 0.26 -> 0.04: both CE Energy News and IBNA (Aug 2) report Bulgaria's Energy Ministry confirming Kozloduy Units 5 & 6 operate normally via their deep-bay pumping station and will not need significant output cuts for at least three weeks despite Serbian Djerdap hydro dropping to 20-30%. Slovenia (0.015) and Switzerland (0.005) trim accordingly (sum 0.99).

questions.title: Which stadium will Shakhtar Donetsk announce an agreement to use for its home matches in the main phase of the 2026–27 UEFA Champions League?
questions.background: War has prevented Shakhtar Donetsk from hosting European matches in Ukraine, forcing the club to arrange alternative venues abroad.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official Shakhtar Donetsk announcement, or reliable reporting quoting the club, identifying its agreed home venue for the 2026–27 Champions League main phase. Resolution Conditions : Resolve to the stadium named in the first such agreement announced by August 31, 2026. The announcement determines the answer; subsequent regulatory approval or the actual staging of matches is not required. Accepted Answer Format : The stadium’s name.
questions.current_reasoning: Complete venue overhaul driven by June 24 - July 26 reporting (BBC Sport, City AM, The Athletic via talkSPORT, Evening Standard, and UNN/Suspilne Sport): Shakhtar officially stated they are negotiating with venues in the UK and Germany (dropping Poland after Wisla Krakow's refusal), and on July 26 Shakhtar head coach Arda Turan explicitly announced 'It looks like we will play our European Cup matches in London... We are also waiting for everyone in London.' Three West London Premier League clubs with no 2026-27 European football have held talks: Brentford's Gtech Community Stadium (0.28 — earliest/longest-documented talks since June 24, established third-party rental model, UEFA compliant), Chelsea's Stamford Bridge (0.26 — 40k turnkey UCL venue, Chelsea seeking non-European revenue after finishing 10th), and Fulham's Craven Cottage (0.23 — renovated Riverside Stand and strong Shakhtar-Fulham relationship from the Kevin transfer). Keeping Veltins-Arena (0.06) as the top German fallback if London policing/council permits stall, and London Stadium (0.04) as an unconfirmed London UEFA Cat 4 fallback with West Ham in the Championship (sum 0.87, leaving 13% for other German/London venues).

questions.title: Which club will sign Djed Spence on a permanent transfer from Tottenham Hotspur during summer 2026?
questions.background: Djed Spence is a Tottenham Hotspur player.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official announcement from Tottenham Hotspur or the receiving club confirming a completed permanent transfer. Resolution Conditions : Resolve to the club that signs Djed Spence directly from Tottenham Hotspur on a permanent transfer between June 1 and August 31, 2026. Loan agreements and unconfirmed transfer reports do not count. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the receiving club.
questions.current_reasoning: Key July 26-28 update from Gianluca Di Marzio (via Football.London and Liverpool.com July 28) and Football365 (July 26): Di Marzio confirms Inter Milan is the ONLY club to have formally contacted Tottenham for Djed Spence during and after the World Cup, keeping Inter clearly #1 (Inter's July 30 free signing of CB John Stones does not fill their Dumfries RWB vacancy). However, Di Marzio reports Spurs hiked their valuation from EUR 30m to >EUR 40m (£35m-£42m) and Roberto De Zerbi is undecided on selling, explicitly warning 'I don't think that Inter Milan wants to spend all that money for a player in that position,' while Football365 notes Inter have begun scouting alternative RWBs—trimming Inter from 0.46 -> 0.42. Everton drop 0.20 -> 0.16 with Di Marzio confirming zero formal contact and Spurs insider John Wenham dismissing Everton's willingness to pay £40m for a right-back. Adding Liverpool at 0.06 (replacing silent Roma at 0.03; linked by Football365/Liverpool.com and financially capable of meeting a £35m-£40m fee), trimming quiet Juventus 0.06 -> 0.04, holding Newcastle United at 0.04, and widening the residual to 0.28 for unlinked Premier League or late-window European clubs if Inter walk away.
